analysis.summary: F-TEST-002: the dashboard has zero component tests. The plan task names four targets — EmptyState, SettingsSheet (DELETE confirm), escapeCSV, and App/tab shell — but the existing escapeCSV coverage in tests/unit/csv-export.test.js already satisfies one of the four. Net new coverage is therefore three test files (or one file with three describe blocks): empty-state.test.jsx, settings-sheet.test.jsx, app-tabs.test.jsx. All three need @testing-library/react and chrome.* / fetch stubs to mount SettingsSheet and App without hitting IndexedDB or the live geolocation client.
analysis.details: EmptyState is a 60-line function component with no side effects, so its test is trivial: render, assert the headline ('No Tracking Detected Yet') and a couple of step labels. SettingsSheet is more involved: 8 useState hooks, two useEffects that fire on open (loadStorageInfo, loadBuildInfo, loadPrivacySettings), and a confirm-clear flow gated by confirmText === 'DELETE' (SettingsSheet.jsx:122). The test must stub chrome.storage.local, fetch('/build-info.json'), clearAllData (db), checkStorageQuota (db), getGeoOptIn and setGeoOptIn. The App.jsx tab test is the most ambitious: App.jsx (485 lines) uses useLiveQuery from dexie-react-hooks, so the db helpers (getFootprints, getStats, calculatePlatformStats) need to be stubbed. After stubbing, render App, click each tab, and assert the corresponding tabpanel id appears. Acceptable: a slimmed App shell with stubbed children, or a 'tab shell' that just exercises the four <button role="tab"> elements and active state. Recommendation: a single new test file at tests/unit/dashboard.test.jsx with three describe blocks. Adds @testing-library/react + @testing-library/jest-dom as devDependencies. Verification per the issue body: `npm run test:run` includes a dashboard test file.
